strongestWhy: B pairs the fullest answer to the owner's actual complaints (every cut becomes a move, real archival furniture for the hyper-detail ask, press-down grades against stack-up dollars, a two-second register) with the only honest engineering plan for it. It alone identifies that the citywide and hydePark frames are separately pre-projected coordinate spaces and makes reprojection the budgeted first gate with a per-frame hard-cut fallback, so its continuous camera is a plan rather than a hope. It gets the codebase facts right (five merged data-gfill paths, 694 untouched tap targets, filters never near the tap layer), rations tilt to three events so 3D stays an event rather than a texture, hard-forces ch4 flat through the dim flag, keeps every state discrete for reduced-motion parity, and ships in three gates where a partial build is still coherent. D is the safer chassis (FLIP camera, containing-block discipline) but retains the hard cross-frame cuts the audit itself flagged; B removes them and says exactly what that costs.
fatalFlaws: A: The signature act1 move, one continuous viewBox zoom from citywide into the township frame, is unbuildable as written. The two frames are separately pre-projected sheets sharing one SVG plane (citywide viewBox 530 -190 1132 1845, hydePark 580 230 1128 765, sibling layers toggled per frame), so tweening between their viewBoxes sweeps across misregistered geometry; A never mentions or budgets the required reprojection.

A: The 18deg tilted first paint with all SVG map labels hidden during tilt yields a label-less opening frame, and anchoring the citywide-gap dollar tower at the Loop pins a non-geographic aggregate to a specific place, brushing the real-data rule it otherwise honors.

B: The entire continuous camera hangs on the reprojection precondition; if that gate slips, the concept degrades to today's hard cuts and most of its visitor-impact claims evaporate. Its 30deg desktop finale tilt is past the range where SVG type stays legible (its own risk list caps mobile at 20deg for exactly this reason).

C: Specs four merged grade fills, four filters, and four depth tokens, but StageBase renders five (GRADES A, B, C, D, U), so the ungraded areas fall out of the depth system and the one-token-per-grade contract is wrong on day one. The 64px relay bar also eats mobile viewport, which C itself flags without resolving.

D: Keeps hard cuts between the citywide and township frame families, the exact nothing-ever-zooms complaint in the audit, dressed as plate changes but not removed; and it is internally inconsistent at ch8, spotlighting the Hyde Park-Kenwood plan area while simultaneously gating renewal-boundary geometry on provenance (the spotlight hole needs the same unsourced geometry).

E: Same five-versus-four grade-fill miscount as C. Its isometric-drawn dollar prisms ride a CSS-perspective-tilted plane, mixing two projections without the single-lean rule C uses to solve exactly this clash. At ch4 it leaves the press filters rendered under the dim field rather than forcing them off, so relief can ghost through the memorial.

F: The load-bearing claim, viewBox fixed at citywide forever with one transform rig, is unbuildable as described. The township chapters depend on the hydePark frame's own gradeFills, lake, and 55 park polygons, which live in a different pre-projected space, and F never mentions reprojection; citywide path detail is also too coarse for its claimed 4x-8x pushes. Adding the whisper section grid to ch4 alters the memorial the brief says stays undecorated. Five-versus-four miscount, and a 10deg tilted SSR first paint risks the opening reading as broken rather than arresting.

It correctly counts the five merged grade-fill paths (geometry.json has A/B/C/D/U; A, C, and D all say four). Its FLIP hybrid camera (compositor transform tween, then snap to the true viewBox on transitionend) is the only camera engine that avoids both per-frame repaint of 900+ paths and Safari's blurry rasterization at rest, which A merely caps and C ignores. It is the only concept that flags the CSS-perspective containing-block trap that would silently break the sticky stage. It honestly gates the one unsourced layer (the renewal boundary ships only with provenance), rations tilt to four beats so the historian register survives, keeps ch4 motionless by moving the camera at ch3, and names the real cost that the verify suite must learn CameraState. Its impact ceiling is slightly lower than A or D, but every numbered item in the owner's audit has a concrete, buildable fix, and the gap to spectacle closes cleanly by grafting the steal list (C's press articulation, D's semantic zoom, F's deed-stack countability, A's title block) onto B's chassis. A is the close second: highest craft and the unique single-lean rule against double-projection, but its fill miscount, un-gated renewal-boundary spotlight, and per-state inverse label counter-scaling make it the riskier build.

It has the correct 3D geometry where it matters (dollar towers as counter-rotated HTML standing off the preserve-3d plane, not fake in-plane axonometry like A and D), the sharpest two-second register answer (the union band as the dock itself, with the five-lane wall drawing the relay via baton verticals and a derived sixth row), and real spectacle that stays in the historian register (THE PRESS at a3-s2, the wet-ink flood with a continuous pull-back in true filing order, the cross-section climb chart). Its semantic zoom for the 32 bombings is the most honest fix for the sub-2px knot. Crucially, its single resolved-states table snapshotted by the verify suite converts the owner's 'check every map' into a diffable artifact, and its risk section includes a tested Safari fallback and an explicit cut order under scope pressure. Its one real gap, the act1 push into the second-coordinate-frame township, is bounded and fixable by grafting D's reprojection precondition or A's second-sheet device. C is cleaner on compliance but rations the 3D to two beats and risks re-triggering the 'boring' verdict; F is the most buildable but the least arresting; D is the most cinematic but carries a real-data violation and the round's biggest engineering bet.

E: The register wall's drawn handoffs are factually wrong: covenants end 1948 but renewal does not begin until 1952, and the code ends 1950 but contract selling starts 1952, so both named drop-lines connect a dying instrument to a successor that was not yet running, which would draw a false claim on a page governed by real-data-only. Act4 also spotlights 'inside the renewal boundary,' geometry not in the verified materials. And the camera-by-wrapper-scaling mechanism with a 3.5x cap cannot reach Binga's-block legibility from an 1132-wide viewBox and has the worst Safari rasterization story of the six.

Pitch rationed to four beats plus retained hard frame cuts leaves the least spectacle in the round for an owner who said go all out; the dock ribbon that only grows as far as the story's current era risks reading as an unfinished render rather than a device; and keeping the ch5 citywide knot 'deliberately' a knot half-cures audit item 3 until its mid-south-side camera arrives.
